cases.reason: The words differ only in the referenced clause number, but the referenced 2002 clause 14.6.6 rule 2 does not exclude a floating-point literal from the composite; 2023 14.7.7 rule 2 a)/b) does (it adds 'a floating-point literal' and standard floating-point usages). 2002 has floating-point numeric literals (8.3.1.2.2.2), so `ADD 1.234567890123456789E0 TO X` with X PIC 9(18)V9(13) has a 2002 composite of 18 integer + 18 fraction = 36 digits (the literal's value equals its significand at E0, so the superimposition is unambiguous) and violates the 2002 rule; the compiler accepts and runs it at --std 2002 exactly as at 2023, while it rejects the same literal written fixed-point (COBOL0805, 36 digits).
cases.needs: its own verdict: the compiler's behaviour at --std 2002 for a floating-point literal operand is wrong (excluded from the composite as in 2023); after the fix, a 2002 witness for that case and for a CD-resident operand

The VALUE format 4 text, GROUP INDICATE, PRESENT WHEN and the report OCCURS DEPENDING suppression are the same in both editions (diffed 13.16.26/13.18.28, 13.16.39/13.18.41). But the GROUP INDICATE suppression the rule invokes is reset by 'any control break' (GI GR1c), and in 2002 a control may be a subscripted table element: 2002 CONTROL SR3 says only 'Data-name-1 may be qualified' and 5.1.3 admits subscription, while 2023 CONTROL SR3 forbids any OCCURS. The compiler refuses every report with a subscripted control at --std 2002 (refute-t-erased/gen_subctl.cob: COBOL1699 citing the 2023 SR3), so the GI-suppression arm of this rule has no 2002 behaviour for such reports. The rule's own content is uniform over the control form. Settle it the same way as q-21 GR5/GR8: if a removed operand form reaches a rule that is uniform over it, OVERTURNED removed-form; otherwise UPHELD.

cases.reason: The reader checked only that CONTROL has the same GENERAL FORMAT, and it does. The syntax rules differ. Sub-item c) prints, at the first GENERATE, 'each control heading ... in order from major to minor (See 13.16.15, CONTROL clause)', and the set of controls is wider in 2002. 2002 CONTROL SR3 says only that data-name-1 may be qualified, a 2002 data-name operand includes subscription (5.1.3; 2014 E.2), and a table element reference shall be subscripted (8.4.1.2.2 SR5). 2023 SR3 forbids any OCCURS. So 'RD R-G CONTROLS ARE FINAL WS-K(1)' with CH/CF WS-K(1) is a legal 2002 report whose first GENERATE this rule governs, and the 2023 row cannot reach it. This is the same family as the q-21 overturn of TYPE GR6 c)/e). A second, lesser reach: a 2002 control may also be a CD record item (CONTROL SR2 excludes only the report section). The compiler does that one correctly: gen_cdctl.cob at 2002 prints [RH] [PH 1] [CHF] [CHK A] [DE A 1]..., identical to the WS twin.

cases.reason: The INSPECT formats and operand numbering are the same in both editions (2023 adds BACKWARD, a widening). In 2002, though, every identifier the rule names may be a record item under a CD: 2002 INSPECT SR1 and SR2 restrict only class and usage, not section, and A.1.1.2 makes CD records ordinary record description entries. 2023 has no such entries. The pointer row does not record this rule as untestable. It is CONFORMS with goldens that pin a documented implementor choice for TALLYING (D-INS1), all in working storage. So the 2002 scope has a part the pointer's evidence never shows. This is the class the reader itself applied to CANCEL GR1, DIVIDE GR4-6 and EVALUATE GR2 in this slice, and the reader did not apply it here. The compiler is correct: insp_cd.cob (operands in a CD record) at 2002 gives D1=[5AAAAA] D2=[31A1A1], identical to its WS twin insp_ws.cob at 2002 and 2023 and to the pb1907 goldens.
